headline.purpose: Modal titles, card section headings, step wizard titles. Compact but authoritative.

title.purpose: Module card names, data card headers, confirmation screen titles. Primary visual anchor within a card.

body.purpose: Module descriptions, modal messages, helper text, how-to steps. Max 65ch on prose surfaces.

label.purpose: Form field labels, table column headers, step badge text. Always uppercase, always short (under 4 words), always 700 weight.

data.purpose: All financial amounts, account codes, document numbers, elapsed timers, bank codes. The switch to mono signals this value must be verified.

shadows.name: shadow-xs
shadows.purpose: Micro-lift for small UI elements: file-info strips, row-count badges, small tool buttons.

shadows.name: shadow-sm
shadows.purpose: Default card shadow. Module cards and panel cards at rest.

shadows.name: shadow-md
shadows.purpose: Hover state on cards, document preview toolbar, floating tool buttons.

shadows.name: shadow-lg
shadows.purpose: Hover state on elevated cards, dropdowns, active-step pulse animation.

shadows.name: shadow-xl
shadows.purpose: Modals and loading overlays. Maximum depth in the system.

shadows.name: shadow-primary
shadows.purpose: Exclusive to primary buttons and the active step indicator. Carmen Blue ambient glow.

shadows.name: shadow-teal
shadows.purpose: Exclusive to the success/teal button variant. Process Teal ambient glow.

shadows.name: panel-card-inset
shadows.purpose: Panel-card and data-card default. Multi-layer outer shadow with inset top-edge highlight.

motion.name: ease-expo-out
motion.purpose: Default easing for all state transitions. Matches --ease in base.css.

motion.name: ease-drawer
motion.purpose: Panel and drawer slide-in. Heavier deceleration than standard.

motion.name: dur-fast
motion.purpose: Micro-interactions: button active scale, icon hover, row highlight.

motion.name: dur-base
motion.purpose: Standard transition duration. Button hover, card hover, border color shifts.

motion.name: dur-slow
motion.purpose: Larger state changes: modal entry, step wizard transition, panel fade.

motion.name: fade-up
motion.purpose: Page-level content entrance. Used on .app-container and .main-content.

motion.name: modal-scale-in
motion.purpose: Modal box entrance. The only scale-from-center animation in the system.

motion.name: shimmer
motion.purpose: Exclusive to the 3px top-edge loading stripe on the OCR overlay and extraction status strip.

motion.name: pulse-ring
motion.purpose: Active step panel-card outline pulse. Communicates that this panel is awaiting user action.

breakpoints.name: mobile-sm
breakpoints.purpose: Compact padding, single-column layout, simplified header.

breakpoints.name: mobile
breakpoints.purpose: Step wizard collapses to number-only; upload grid becomes 1-column; modal actions stack.

breakpoints.name: tablet
breakpoints.purpose: 44px minimum tap targets enforced; preview height caps at 45vh.

breakpoints.name: tablet-lg
breakpoints.purpose: Upload section grid transitions from 3 to 2 columns.

breakpoints.name: desktop
breakpoints.purpose: Main content grid switches from 1-column to 2-column; preview column becomes sticky.

narrative.overview:
Carmen AI Automation is a tool where the stakes are real: extracted numbers go directly into GL entries. The interface treats every pixel as a readout, not a decoration. Surfaces recede. Headers read like panel labels. Numeric values surface in monospace, unambiguous. Motion conveys state, not atmosphere. The tool is precise because the work demands precision.

The system rejects the SaaS playbook entirely. There are no gradient text treatments, no hero metrics with big numbers and gradient accents, no celebratory animations for routine accounting tasks, and no enterprise-legacy chrome. The palette is restrained: one brand accent used as a state indicator, not an identity statement. Color communicates "this needs your attention" or "this is confirmed" — never "look how polished we are."

Thai and English are equally considered. Sarabun sits alongside Inter in every font stack. Vendor names, GL labels, and invoice text arrive in Thai; every layout decision accounts for it.
keyCharacteristics: Surfaces recede; data leads. Card chrome is minimal so extracted values stand forward.
Mono for amounts, Inter/Sarabun for everything else. The distinction is structural.
Color = state. Carmen Blue signals the active action or current step. Color signals state, never mood.
Dark mode is first-class. Every token has a dark variant; no surfaces use raw hex.
Workflow-first layout. Every screen belongs to a step in the document-processing flow.
44px minimum tap targets on mobile. Accounting tools are used on tablets.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Carmen Blue appears on ≤15% of any given screen. When every action and every active state wears the same color, that color retains its signal value. Do not use Carmen Blue for decorative gradients, section dividers, or inactive-state backgrounds.

rules.name: The No-Raw-Hex Rule
rules.body: All color values must reference a CSS custom property from :root. Dark mode works because every token has a [data-theme='dark'] override. Never hardcode oklch() or hex values in component code.

rules.name: The Mono Signal Rule
rules.body: IBM Plex Mono appears only on values the user must verify: amounts, codes, dates, status strings, elapsed timers. It does not appear on headings, button labels, or descriptive text. If a piece of text is in mono, it is data.

rules.name: The Scale Ceiling Rule
rules.body: No heading in the product exceeds clamp(2.1rem, 5vw, 2.6rem) (the home page h1). Module-internal headings are capped at 1.1rem. Product UI does not shout; it organizes.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Shadows appear only on surfaces that contain or represent interactive content. Purely structural surfaces (dividers, separators, empty containers) are flat. A shadow is a promise that something is interactive or elevated.

rules.name: The One-Layer-of-Blur Rule
rules.body: Backdrop blur is reserved for the sticky app-header (14px), modal overlays (16px), toast containers (16px), and the OCR loading overlay (8px). Never applied to cards, panels, or inline UI.

dos: Do use IBM Plex Mono for every financial amount, account code, document number, and date value.
Do give every interactive element a focus-visible ring: outline 2.5px solid var(--primary) with outline-offset 2px.
Do reference CSS custom properties for every color — never raw hex or oklch in component code.
Do use the 44px minimum tap target for all buttons on mobile.
Do apply @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) for every animation.
Do apply text-wrap: balance on headings and text-wrap: pretty on modal messages.
Do treat the step wizard as the primary navigation metaphor on all module screens.
Do verify Ink Tertiary contrast on every new surface — it borders WCAG AA at the body text floor.
Do include all five button states in every new button variant: default, hover, focus, active, disabled.
Do use the Sarabun font stack on every text element that may contain Thai script.
donts: Don't add background-clip: text with a gradient background. Gradient text is prohibited.
Don't use border-left or border-right greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe — the existing toast is a legacy issue, not a template.
Don't use backdrop-filter: blur on cards, panel surfaces, or inline UI elements.
Don't introduce a display font. Inter handles all hierarchy within this product.
Don't add a flash AI SaaS aesthetic: no hero-metric big-number layouts, no gradient accents, no celebration animations.
Don't use Carmen Blue on more than 15% of a given screen surface.
Don't use modal-first for actions where an inline confirmation or toast would work.
Don't hardcode raw hex or rgba values in new component code — dark mode breaks on raw values.
Don't ship a new workflow screen without empty states for tables and data columns.
Don't animate layout properties (width, height, top, left). Animate transform and opacity only.
